title: Fennel and the Big Rainbow of Feelings
subtitle: A story about all our feelings
subtitle_listing: A Story About All Our Feelings
story: Rain tapped the window. Rain tapped the door.
Fennel stayed in. What was in store?
top
Mama set nine jars down in a row,
each with a small light, glowing aglow.
top
Red for his Mad, a balloon that grew.
Blue for his Sad, a puddle, too.
top
Gray for his Worry, a tangle of thread.
Green for his Jealous, a vine in his head.
top
Orange for Scared, a spark in the night.
Peach for his Shy, a cloud, soft and light.
top
Yellow for Excited, all bounce and zing.
Purple for Frustrated, a tight little spring.
top
Teal for his Lonely, a bubble so round.
Nine feelings, each one, he had found.
top
“Feelings come, and feelings go.
Each one helps us learn and grow.”
top
“Feel it. Name it. Share it, too.
That’s all you need. That’s all you do.”
top
He told Papa Bear, “I felt scared last night.”
“Me too,” said Papa, and they hugged tight.
top
The rain slowed down. The clouds rolled away.
The sun peeked out on a bright new day.
top
A rainbow stretched out, from jar to jar.
Every feeling is part of who we are.
top

listing.description:
It is a rainy day, and Mama Bear brings out nine glowing jars. Each one holds a feeling Fennel has met.

A red balloon for his Mad. A blue puddle for his Sad. A gray tangle of worry, a green vine of jealous, an orange spark of scared, a peach cloud of shy, yellow sparks of excited, a purple spring of frustrated, and a teal bubble of lonely.

With three feeling steps — Feel it. Name it. Share it. — little readers learn that every feeling is okay and part of who we are, until the rain stops and a rainbow stretches from jar to jar.

Inside this warm rhyming picture book:

  • A cozy read-aloud rhyme for ages 3–6 that celebrates all nine feelings from the series
  • A kid-friendly image for every feeling, shown as a glowing jar
  • Three easy steps children can copy: Feel it, Name it, Share it
  • A note for grown-ups with simple ways to talk about feelings every day
  • Soft watercolor-style illustrations

Book 10 in the Fennel's Feelings series. A gentle finale, and a great place for a new reader to begin.
